MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r3.claim: At dawn the owners called to one another.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r5.claim: At daybreak the brothers called one another to go harvest the fruit.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r7.claim: At daybreak, they called one another.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r1.claim: تنادوا means the brothers called one another to go to their appointment.

TABRISI:68:17-33/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:17-33/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:17-33/r5.claim: The brothers called one another in the morning; the term for calling derives from extended voiced sound, as the throat's moisture lets a person's voice carry.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#3/r1.claim: When morning came, the owners called to one another.

RAZI-FULL:v30p78#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#3/r1.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#3/r1.claim: Muqātil says that at morning they urged each other to go to their fields of fruit, crops, and grapes to cut the produce.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r5.claim: They called one another early and told each other to set out for the crop; على implies approaching it or likens dawn harvest to an attacking force, and صرمين means reapers.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p270/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270/r1.claim: At morning, some called out to the others.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r7.claim: The owners called one another to proceed to the appointed time for their harvest.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196/r1.claim: At daybreak they called one another to go harvest if they intended to reap the crop.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p105/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p105/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p105/r1.claim: Their resolve made them act as if they had arranged a meeting: they called to one another at the first part of morning.

BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r6.claim: The owners called one another at dawn and urged an early start.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#6/r1.claim: They called to one another in the morning, in keeping with their earlier oath.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r4.claim: Calling it their own cultivation assumes sole ownership; عَلَىٰ حَرْثِكُمْ evokes attacking and cutting it down as if striking an enemy.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r4.claim: Calling one another suggests urging each other to go early; غدو means leaving at the start of the day.

TABATABAI:68:20-28/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r4.claim: They called to one another at daybreak to go early to the orchard and harvest if they were intent on cutting its fruit; aghdu means go early, with an implicit sense of approaching that explains ala rather than ila.

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.claim: Exegetes elaborate the garden story: it belonged to a righteous man who left it to his people and town; reports place it in Yemen near Ṣanʿāʾ, Abyssinia, or among the People of Scripture.

STUDYQURAN:68:17/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r8.claim: The brothers’ exclusion of the poor violated an ancient Near Eastern custom allowing the poor to glean and the Quranic command to give the harvest due on harvest day.
